newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end at session highs on Btps, lira.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end at session highs on Btps, lira.

text.p: Italian shares ended an active session at the day's highs on Thursday, boosted by surging Italian Btp futures and the lira which both peaked at new highs, traders said.
The lira touched 989.80 against the mark, a new two year high, and the December Btp future contract rose to a record 124.13. But both lira and futures settled back at the close.
"With Italian debt instruments and the currency at these levels the stock market could even do a bit more," one Milan trader said.
The all-share Mibtel index ended 1.51 pct up at 10,299 and the Mib30 blue chip index closed 1.61 pct higher at 15,538.

Troubled high-tech group Olivetti was off 0.5 percent at 517.7 lire ahead of a meeting with analysts. News CEO Roberto Colaninni said the group aimed to divest its PC business and other units by the end of 1996 came after the market closed.

State energy group ENI closed 2.08 percent down at 7,529 against the trendr. Traders said the fall could be due to selling ahead of a second tranche share placement later this month with a view to buying back at lower levels.
Financial holding company Gemina rose 6.56 percent to 760.2 amid talk it might be about to announce a sale or an investment in the industrial sector.
Telecoms, banks and insurances were generally firm.
Provisional estimates put trading volume at over 900 billion lire against Wednesday's 648 billion.
